desc:
Ecommerce dashboards in Looker Studio put your sales, products and marketing results on one page that updates by itself. Ecom Swift LLC connects your store, analytics and ad accounts, then builds charts in plain words that match your sources.

## What is an ecommerce dashboard?

An ecommerce dashboard is a single page that pulls live figures from your store, analytics and ad accounts into charts and scorecards. It answers the questions you ask every morning: how much did we sell, what sold, where did visitors come from and what did ads cost. Looker Studio is a free reporting tool from Google that connects to many sources, which makes it a practical home for this.

The alternative is opening five logins, exporting spreadsheets and pasting numbers together. That takes time, invites mistakes and often stops after a few weeks.

## Why a shared view of the numbers helps the business

A dashboard saves time, but its bigger value is agreement. When the owner, the marketer and the bookkeeper all look at the same page, discussions start from the same facts. Nobody has to ask which spreadsheet is current.

It also changes how quickly you notice problems. A drop in orders, a spike in ad spend or a product that suddenly stops selling is visible on the day, not at month end. Trends become easier to read when charts compare this week with last week, or this month with the same month a year earlier.

A dashboard does not make decisions for you. It makes the right questions easier to ask, and it shows whether last week's change moved anything.

## What a good dashboard contains

- A top row of scorecards: revenue, orders, average order value and conversion rate.
- A date range picker and a comparison switch, so any period can be set against another.
- A sales trend chart that shows daily or weekly movement without clutter.
- A top products table with units sold and revenue.
- Traffic by source, so you can see which channels bring visitors and orders.
- Ad spend next to the sales it is linked to, by platform.
- Customer views, such as new against returning buyers.
- Plain labels, with a short note on what each number means and where it comes from.
- Filters for country, device or channel where they help.
- Consistent colors and spacing, so the page reads at a glance on a laptop or phone.

## How we build your dashboard

We start by choosing the questions the dashboard must answer, since the charts follow from them. A store owner who checks daily wants a very different page from an agency preparing monthly updates.

Next we connect the data sources. Google Analytics, Google Ads, Search Console and Google Sheets connect directly. For stores on Shopify, WooCommerce and other platforms, we use a connector or a scheduled export so sales flow in without manual work. Meta and TikTok results can come through a connector too. We explain what each connector costs, if anything, before we use it.

Then we build the pages, label every chart in plain language and check each figure against its source. If the dashboard shows a different revenue figure from your store, we find the reason, for example tax, shipping or refunds counted differently, and note it on the page. Basic gives you one clean page. Standard adds more pages and sources. Premium adds targets, a weekly emailed copy, and a training video with a written guide.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Start with a few charts you will actually read.
- Put the most important number at the top left.
- Give each chart a title that says what it shows.
- Keep sharing settings tight, and remove people who leave your team.
- Check dashboard totals against your store every month.

**Avoid:**
- Adding every available metric because it is possible.
- Mixing different date ranges on one page without saying so.
- Using vague names such as "performance" or "stats".
- Connecting a source nobody understands.
- Treating a number as final before checking its source.

## Who a dashboard is for

This service suits owners who spend time each week collecting figures by hand and want that time back. It suits small teams where marketing, operations and finance each use different tools, and agencies that need a clear client view. It also helps a store that has just fixed its tracking and wants a good place to read the results.

## What we need from you

Tell us which accounts to connect: your store, Google Analytics, ad platforms and any sheets you keep. We need viewer or analyst access to those accounts, and editor access to Looker Studio is created in your own Google account so you own the dashboard. A list of the questions you want answered and any brand colors or logo help us finish the design. We never need passwords, and you decide who can view the report.
